Methodology

How the ledger is kept.

  1. Prices come only from each vendor’s own pricing page. Each row stores the source URL and check date.
  2. A row is verified when the figure was read on that date. We never estimate a missing price.
  3. Estimated monthly cost = base + user overage (MAU/MRU bands) + SSO connection fees from the published ladder. Logto token overage is noted but not assumed from MAU.
  4. SSO users per connection (assumption). Amazon Cognito, Supabase Auth and Firebase Auth / Identity Platform bill SAML/OIDC per SSO user, not per connection (first 50 free, then $0.015 per SSO user a month). To compare them with per-connection vendors we assume 200 SSO users per connection by default; you can change it in the calculator. We also count those users inside your total MAU, which can slightly overstate these vendors above their free direct-user allowance; we keep the higher figure. Sensitivity, computed from the same ledger rows (cheapest plan, monthly, rank among all priceable plans):

  5. Headline number. At 100k users, Clerk Pro lists $1,025/mo; WorkOS AuthKit, the cheapest verified plan that includes MFA at that size, lists $0 ($12,300/yr less). We compare a named, popular plan with the cheapest verified plan that includes MFA at the same user count (no SSO), because that is a saving a team can actually capture. The max-minus-min spread across all 13 plans priced at 50k users · 5 SSO is $26,817/yr (Descope Pro vs Firebase Auth / Identity Platform Pay as you go, the latter assumes 200 SSO users per connection); we keep it here only, since nobody chooses between those two.
  6. Ties and precision. Plans at the same price are shown as ties (for example “tie at $0”), never as wins or ordinal ranks. Rates show the precision the vendor publishes (for example Supabase $0.00325 per MAU).
  7. Auth0 sells paid plans in published MAU tiers (B2C to 50k, B2B to 20k, from auth0.com/pricing.md); usage between tiers is priced at the next tier up, as Auth0 bills it. Above the top tier only Enterprise (contact sales) remains, so we omit Auth0 there rather than invent a number. Correction 2026-10-31: before that date we wrongly treated tiers above 500 MAU as custom.
  8. Stytch MAU overage rate was not printed as a fixed USD figure on the checked page — left blank.
  9. A weekly script diffs every source page; confirmed changes enter the price log.
